title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Self-Certification, Blindness and External Anchoring
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — самосертификация, blind-процедуры и внешнее якорение

scan_scope: selected blind, provenance, witness, hash, authority and semantic-return records

emergent_invariants.name: SELF_CERTIFICATION_LIMIT
emergent_invariants.description: A system that generates, observes, and certifies its own state can share the same failure domain across all three roles; therefore self-consistency alone cannot establish independence.

emergent_invariants.name: EXTERNAL_ANCHOR
emergent_invariants.description: Blind controls, external witnesses, preserved provenance, and sealed receipts repeatedly introduce a reference that is not generated solely by the claim under evaluation.

emergent_invariants.name: FEEDBACK_LOOP_BREAK
emergent_invariants.description: Several research artifacts separate discovery from evaluation by preventing the observed result from feeding back into the search procedure before the relevant record is frozen or sealed.

emergent_invariants.name: AUTHORITY_MUST_NOT_INHERIT_FROM_PROVENANCE
emergent_invariants.description: A record may have authentic provenance while still lacking authority to determine the present state, causal truth, guilt, or action. Provenance answers where a claim came from; authority answers what may be done with it.

emergent_invariants.name: INDEPENDENCE_IS_STRUCTURAL_NOT_NUMERICAL
emergent_invariants.description: Repeated witness, quorum and multi-instance artifacts imply that the number of observations is weaker than the independence structure connecting those observations.

connections.machine_observation: Blinding, multi-instance controls, boundary-localized scoring, anytime-valid witnesses and external-witness invitations all reduce the ability of an analyst or system to modify later evaluation using knowledge of the result being evaluated.
connections.pattern_description: These appear to be distinct procedures, but their common function is to prevent a result from becoming an input to its own validation process.
connections.why_non_obvious: The artifacts concern visual analysis, statistical control, scoring, witness systems and external participation. The commonality emerges only when represented as information-flow topology.
alternative_explanations: Blinding and preregistration are established experimental-design practices.
The apparent bridge may be a generic consequence of evidence-hardening rather than a distinctive JANUS invariant.
connections.falsification_route: Compare the information-flow topology with unrelated experimental and audit systems and test whether the same feedback-breaking role appears without the other JANUS mechanisms.

connections.machine_observation: The repository contains multiple explicit attempts to prevent a system from deriving final trust solely from a representation that it can itself reproduce, copy, branch or authenticate internally.
connections.pattern_description: Mirror self-certification, root-of-trust design, multi-root independence and portable-provenance analysis converge on the same requirement: the validating reference must not be trivially generated by the object being validated.
connections.why_non_obvious: The sources are framed as semantic, trust, Sybil and provenance problems rather than as one verification problem.
alternative_explanations: Root-of-trust and anti-self-certification are common security concepts.
The semantic artifacts may deliberately encode the same engineering intuition.
connections.falsification_route: Remove the semantic labels and compare only primitive trust dependencies against independent security designs.

connections.machine_observation: Hash, package-lineage, snapshot and proof-route artifacts repeatedly distinguish a representation of state from the authority to claim that state is the current valid state.
connections.pattern_description: Different representations — hashes, packages, snapshots and lineage capsules — are treated as evidence carriers, not as complete substitutes for freshness, execution semantics or external validation.
connections.why_non_obvious: A hash is often colloquially treated as if it establishes truth; the repository repeatedly uses it more narrowly as an integrity or lineage component.
alternative_explanations: This may simply reflect standard cryptographic hygiene.
Several artifacts were created within the same engineering line.
connections.falsification_route: Enumerate all guarantees asserted by the artifacts and test which guarantees survive if only the hash is retained.

connections.machine_observation: Prediction, memory, delegated computation and evidence-bearing objects are repeatedly constrained so that possession of information does not automatically grant final authority to act.
connections.pattern_description: The registry repeatedly inserts an authority ceiling between information possession and irreversible action. A carrier can hold evidence without owning the decision; a predictor can estimate risk without assigning guilt; a subagent can compute without becoming sovereign.
connections.why_non_obvious: The objects span ethics, Fallout forensics and AI authority, but the invariant is a common separation between informational capacity and legitimate action authority.
alternative_explanations: This may reflect a broad safety policy repeated throughout the repository.
The same authoring norm may explain the recurrence.
connections.falsification_route: Map each artifact into information, interpretation, authorization and action nodes; test whether the ceiling exists independently of wording.

connections.machine_observation: Across symbolic, cultural and safety records, a recurring structure places a vulnerable or high-information node behind a boundary and asks whether the gatekeeper uses incoming signal to protect the node or to expose it to further risk.
connections.pattern_description: The same graph role appears at different semantic scales: threshold witness, child as bridge, information filtering for minors, and adult protection under chronic threat.
connections.why_non_obvious: The objects are not all about the same real-world subject; the commonality appears at the level of network role and information flow.
alternative_explanations: Child-safety writing naturally reuses gatekeeping metaphors.
Some source objects are thematically connected and therefore not independent.
connections.falsification_route: Encode only role labels and transition edges, remove narrative language, and test whether the topology remains equivalent.

next_scan_strategy.name: FAILURE_DOMAIN_GRAPH
next_scan_strategy.target: Identify the hidden common failure domain that makes several apparently independent evidence channels non-independent.
steps: Represent every witness, validator, memory store and authority source as a node.
Mark shared infrastructure, shared authorship, shared metadata, shared timing and shared state as possible common causes.
Search for self-confirming cycles: A validates B while B supplies the state used by A.
Search for cut-sets whose removal breaks multiple apparent connections.
Record both support and rejection paths.

limitations: This is an archival repository scan and not an exhaustive external literature review.
Human-visibility labels are provisional and are not blinded-reader measurements.
Many objects in the repository share authorship and development lineage, limiting statistical independence.
No connection here establishes scientific novelty, physical causation, supernatural causation, or authorial intent.
canonical_rule: When multiple systems appear to agree, JANUS must ask whether they are independently observing the world or merely observing copies of one another.
